messages.subject: New User - Troubleshooting
messages.body_plain:
First of all, thank you for making this tool open-source and providing a Wiki for us to follow. MaAsLin seems like a very useful tool for microbiome analysis but I've spent the past several days attempting to get it up and running with little success. I was hoping you could provide some advice on some issues I've come across. Thank you for your time!

1. Galaxy module:
Does the module have an option for random effects?
Is there an option to force predictors?
Is the server secure for data sets with sensitive data?
How long do jobs typically takes (e.g. I have 533 samples & 5 metadata covariates)?

2. Installation in R:
I ran into an error which states MaAsLin was not available for R version 3.4.4. Which R version would you recommend? I'm currently using the install.package() command as I'm not familiar with the R CMD INSTALL method in Windows.

3. Docker - I successfully ran MaAsLin using Docker. However, my p-values and q-values are outside the normal range (e.g. negative or >1). This seems to be an issue previously reported by several users: https://bitbucket.org/biobakery/maaslin/issues/23/error-reading-p-values-when-using-random. Unfortunately, the solution posted in this site did not appear to work for other users and changing the package version in Docker is not quite straightforward to new users such as myself. Do you have any suggestions?

Thanks,
Kyu

messages.subject: Re: NA/NaN argument error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kyu,

Thanks for your email. Before installing the latest version (0.0.5), did you also install the following R packages with appropriate versions, i.e. agricolae, gam (version 1.14), gamlss, gbm, glmnet, inlinedocs, logging, MASS, nlme (version 3.1-127), optparse, outliers, penalized, pscl, robustbase. If not, you can follow the following pseudo-code to do that before downloading and installing Maaslin:

# Install pacman (to install other packages in one line of code)

if(! require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman", repos='http://cran.us.r-project.org')
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("pacman"))
pacman::p_load('agricolae', 'gamlss', 'gbm', 'nlme', 'gam',
               'glmnet', 'inlinedocs', 'logging', 'devtools',
               'MASS', 'optparse', 'outliers',
               'penalized', 'pscl', 'robustbase')

# Install Older Version of gam
if (!packageVersion('gam')=='1.14') {
  remove.packages('gam')
  devtools::install_version("gam", version = "1.14", repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org")
}

# Install Older Version of nlme
if (!packageVersion('nlme')=='3.1-127') {
  remove.packages('nlme')
  devtools::install_version("nlme", version = "3.1-127", repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org")
}

Please let me know if you have any difficulty with the installation using the above procedure.

Many thanks,
Himel

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I would like to run Maaslin on functional (KEGG) data. I tried in R with this:
Maaslin("patients.tsv", "/Users/stepra/Results/Maaslin/output1", iLastMetadata=5)
but get the following warnings for all samples:

messages.subject: Fixed effects
messages.body_plain:
Hello all.

When I run my dataset (attached) all but one of my metadata categories return results. There is no spreadsheet returned for "Habitat", which unfortunately happens to be the one I'm most interested in! (and the variable that has consistently explained much of the variation in other stats). In exploring this issue I think the solution is to specify habitat as a fixed effect with all others as random, however the argument description (pasted below) was confusing to me. Is strRandomCovariates the argument to specify fixed effects? It seems to say it's both for random and not random covariates...and this was the only argument about fixed or random covariates I could find.

## Fixed (not random) covariates
pArgs <- add_option( pArgs, c("-R","--random"), type="character", action="store", dest="strRandomCovariates", default=lsArgs$strRandomCovariates, metavar="fixed", help="These metadata will be treated as random covariates. Comma delimited data feature names. These features must be listed in the read.config file. Example '-R RandomMetadata1,RandomMetadata2'.  [Default %default]")

Here are things I've tried so far:

        strMultTestCorrection = "BH"
        dSelectionFrequency=1
        dSelectionFrequency=0
        strModelSelection=none

Selection frequency of 1 returned results for Habitat, but left out most of the other variables. All others made no difference. Thank you for your time.

messages.subject: Re: Fixed effects
messages.body_plain:
Hello Mae,

strRandomCovariates refer to the name(s) of the variables that you want to specify as random effects. You may or may not have random effects in your model but by default, every metadata in your metadata is modeled as a fixed effect (unless that metadata is specified as random effects). Let me know if that resolves your confusion.

Many thanks,
Himel

messages.subject: Re: too many low abundance bugs
messages.body_plain:
Hi Stef,

MaAsLin requires the data to be proportional between 0 and 1 for the default linear modeling. If your data is not proportional (which seems to be true in your case), you can still run MaAsLin without worries by specifying strTransform='none', as the default arc-sine square root transformation is not valid for non-proportional values. A similar argument also applies to the default filtering (dMinAbd = 0.0001, dMinSamp = 0.1), which is more appropriate for proportional relative abundance data. You can tune these two parameters according to your filtering need, which should take care of the warnings you are seeing, in addition to ensuring a valid analysis. Let me know if that answers your question.

Many thanks,
Himel

> > From the analysis standpoint, the variables we want to adjust for are those that we are not primarily interested in but we want to include in the model in order to ‘cancel out’ their effect on the primary variables of interest. In that sense, you are absolutely right that one would not expect to see these variables in the output file. But if we carefully look at the statistical model under the hood, those variables are not estimated separately or independently. In fact, they are treated exactly like the primary variables in the model and all the variables are jointly estimated to produce individual coefficient estimates and p-values. That being said, in most practical scenarios, we are not interested in anything beyond our primary variables of interest. This viewpoint is incorporated in many statistical softwares  that allow you to specify your main and adjusting variables separately so that only main variables are included in the output table. MaAsLin does not separate these two  for a couple of reasons: (i) it accommodates the general case of multivariable analysis when users are interested in all the variables, and (ii) users can always subset their output file to the specific variables they are interested in. Note that, these two philosophical differences of reporting significant associations do not undermine the individual p-values and coefficients as they are essentially coming from the exact same multivariable model.

Hello there,

This problem arises if you don't have the correct versions of the required packages. In particular, MaAsLin requires the following R packages: agricolae, gam (version 1.14), gamlss, gbm, glmnet, inlinedocs, logging, MASS, nlme (version 3.1-127), optparse, outliers, penalized, pscl, robustbase. Can you make sure you have the correct versions for nlme and gam? If not, can you try installing the correct versions and re-install MaAsLin and see if the problem still remains?

Many thanks,
